properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform. NOTE: an initial attempt also used the real, confirmed positions of the Sophie Maxwell Building and the UCSF Block 2 building as anchors, but they produced 50-60m of error against the street-only fit -- this diagram is dated Feb 26, 2020, predating UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as a life-science anchor tenant, so those two real buildings likely do not sit where this 2020 figure's own numbered blocks would place them (their own real parcels are used directly elsewhere in this dataset and were NOT re-derived from this diagram). The final transform here uses street intersections only. Residual error against those control points is roughly 8-24m. Traced polygons were additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels (and against Prequel Park's approximate geometry) so this speculative tracing never overrides real or better-sourced geometry. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged pattern of blocks encroaching on real streets across the site (Block 3, Block 11, Block 12) led to rebuilding this whole block layer from scratch using proper GCP-based georeferencing (GDAL's gdaltransform with a thin-plate-spline transform, the same technique QGIS's Georeferencer uses) instead of patching individual curbs. Installed GDAL, computed 8 real street-intersection ground control points from OpenStreetMap data (Craig Lane x Maryland St, 22nd St x Maryland/Louisiana St, Humboldt St x Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane, 23rd St x Maryland/Georgia Lane), precisely located each in the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) via programmatic black-pixel border detection cross-checked with visual ruler crops, and fit a TPS transform. Re-traced this block's own corner pixels the same way and ran them through the new transform. This corrected transform disagrees with the original 9-point affine transform by tens of meters in places -- e.g. it revealed the original trace had Blocks 3/4 shifted east into the excavation pit/street area, and Blocks 11/12 roughly 2x too deep -- and the new positions now land within real, distinct site features (buildings, graded lots) visible in satellite imagery rather than straddling roads. Known residual limitation: GCP street positions are centerline-based (matching OSM convention), while a block boundary should sit at the near curb, so any edge close to a GCP street can land a few meters into that street after transformation -- checked for and corrected on this block's street-facing edge(s) where applicable using this project's already-established grid bearing (356.5 deg) and, where available, an independently diagram-measured depth/width. Treat corrected vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (tighter than the original 8-24m transform, but still not survey-grade). RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (same day, third pass): the independent per-block TPS re-trace (see above) still measured each block's own 4 corners in isolation, which -- despite using the same transform -- left small (3-12m) spurious gaps or misalignments at boundaries the diagram actually draws as shared or tightly-spaced between adjacent blocks (caught after the user pointed out the diagram itself has ~zero wasted space and specifically that the PG&E switchyard polygon sits directly against Block 5 in the diagram, not ~60m away as this dataset had it). Re-measured EVERY block's corners in a single consistent pass using programmatic black-pixel border detection (long contiguous runs = real borders, filtered from text/dimension-arrow strokes by requiring the run to span nearly the full block height/width), cross-validated with fine-pixel-gridline crops, so that shared or consistently-measured boundaries between neighboring blocks now come from the same underlying pixel measurements rather than independent eyeball estimates. Batch-transformed through the same GDAL/TPS fit as before. This pass also corrected several block extents that were measured imprecisely in the prior pass (e.g. Block 5's real stepped/notched south edge, Block 11's true position -- it does NOT sit flush against Block 15, there is real Power Station Park open space between them). GCP CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (fourth pass): user flagged that Block 8/12 should touch Delaware Street with park space between them, and that Block 3/4's shapes looked off -- investigation found the root cause was a single mis-measured ground control point. The 'Delaware St x Humboldt St' GCP used for the whole site's TPS transform had been placed at pixel (2227, 986), which is actually deep inside Building 9's own footprint in the diagram, not on Delaware Street at all -- confirmed by comparing pixel spacing between the three Humboldt-row GCPs (Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane): Maryland-to-Georgia-Lane's pixel:real-world ratio implied Delaware should sit at roughly pixel x=2020, not 2227, and a direct color-transition scan at y=986 confirmed the real street gap is at x=1994-2035. Corrected the GCP to (2015, 986) (same real-world coordinate, just the right pixel) and re-ran the TPS transform for the whole site. This produced large corrections concentrated exactly where the user's complaint pointed -- Block 4 shifted 33-60m, Block 3's east corners ~28-33m, Block 8's east corners ~29-31m, Block 12's east corners ~26-27m -- while blocks far from the error (5, 15, 7, 11, PG&E) shifted well under 5m, consistent with a localized GCP error rather than a global transform problem. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source_doc_urls entry pointed to the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the Design for Development (potrero_power_D4D_draft-082219.pdf), which now returns 404 and has no archive snapshot; it has been repointed to the adopted final D4D (February 26, 2020, https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) and Table 3.1.1 Permitted Uses on printed p.47, and whose footers carry the February 26, 2020 date; the SF Planning project page (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station) is added as the source for status and phasing. The statement above that this diagram predates UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as an anchor tenant is not supported by any source cited on this file: the diagram's February 26, 2020 date is confirmed, but no cited source dates UCSF's arrival, so that part is unsourced. Two more statements in the log above are corrected. (1) Where the log says Block 11 does not sit flush against Block 15 because there is Power Station Park open space between them: in the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3 the green strip between Blocks 15 and 11 is labelled 'LOUISIANA PASEO'; 'POWER STATION PARK' is labelled on the green rectangle between Blocks 7 and 11. (2) Heights for Block 7 were re-read from the figure's colour-coded labels, not its XX'MAX dimension lines: the north-west part of Block 7 (on Humboldt St at Louisiana Paseo) is labelled 240'/85' (240 ft maximum, 85 ft base) and the rest of the block is 85'; the '150'MAX' markings are plan dimensions, not heights. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (real-vs-approximate overlap audit, prompted by a user question about validation consistency): despite this file's own regulatory_context already stating it was 'clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint,' a from-scratch real-vs-approximate overlap check found this polygon still overlapped Sophie Maxwell (blklot 4232020) by 1,082 sq m -- the clip described in that text was apparently never actually applied to (or was lost from) the committed geometry. Re-clipped now via shapely difference() against blklot 4232020's real parcel boundary; area dropped from ~4,965 to ~3,883 sq m. This overlap had gone undetected because check_geometry_quality.py only ever checks approximate-vs-approximate sibling overlaps, never real-vs-approximate ones. The vacant/graded and unaddressed-in-the-Assessor-roll wording is our own observation, not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; 'not yet built' is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says the developer had submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects. The 2020 date of the diagram is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020). DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, most unaddressed; whether one of them corresponds to this block was not checked, so the statement that no subdivided Assessor parcel exists for it is unverified.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn, queried 2026-09-29) shows at least 22 active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 following the Phase 1 Final Map recorded July 26, 2022 (most unaddressed; e.g. 4232022 = 151 Humboldt St, 4232020 = 1212 Maryland St); whether one of them matches this block was not checked.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (listed as 'Block 7' in the final D4D's Table 3.1.1; '(remaining portion)' in the project name is our own label, and SF Planning's design review approval calls this portion Block 7A) -- see accuracy_caveat.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). CLIPPED 2026-09-17: although this record's regulatory notes already said the shape was 'clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint,' a fresh check of overlaps between real parcels and approximate shapes found this polygon still overlapped Sophie Maxwell (block/lot 4232020) by 1,082 sq m -- the clip described in that text was apparently never actually applied to (or was lost from) the published shape. It was then re-clipped against block/lot 4232020's real parcel boundary; area dropped from ~4,965 to ~3,883 sq m. This overlap had gone undetected because Pier & Point's automated shape check only compared approximate shapes with each other, never with real parcels. The vacant/graded and unaddressed-in-the-Assessor-roll wording is our own observation, not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; 'not yet built' is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says the developer had submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects. The 2020 date of the diagram is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020). DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, most unaddressed; whether one of them corresponds to this block was not checked, so the statement that no subdivided Assessor parcel exists for it is unverified.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) shows at least 22 active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 following the Phase 1 Final Map recorded July 26, 2022 (most unaddressed; e.g. 4232022 = 151 Humboldt St, 4232020 = 1212 Maryland St); whether one of them matches this block was not checked.
properties.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 7 as one numbered block, with its height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: the north-west part (on Humboldt St at Louisiana Paseo) is labelled 240'/85' (maximum height 240 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and the rest of the block (east side and south strip) is 85'; the two '150'MAX' markings are plan dimensions of the tower, not heights. The D4D numbers only 'Block 7'; 'Block 7A' and 'Block 7B' are the names SF Planning's own approvals use for the two buildings (e.g. 'Approval of the Design Review Application of Block 7A', March 2, 2022, Case 2017-011878PHA-04, and Block 7B, March 2, 2022). The Sophie Maxwell Building ('Block 7b, the Sophie Maxwell Building' in the 2024 annual compliance report; real blklot 4232020, addressed 1212 MARYLAND in DataSF Parcels; already mapped separately in this dataset) occupies part of this block; this polygon is the REMAINING portion, clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint (the clipping is our own work). The remainder is presumed to correspond to 'Block 7A' (Foster + Partners-designed rental tower, press-reported heights of 240-264 ft depending on source, consistent with this figure's 240 ft max) -- design review approved March 2, 2022; the 2024 annual compliance report says no market-rate building permits had been submitted; no construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (listed as 'Block 7' in the final D4D's Table 3.1.1; '(remaining portion)' in the project name is our own label, and SF Planning's design review approval calls this portion Block 7A) -- see the accuracy note for this shape.
